correctness.rationale: Conditional union probability integrates to the difference of the two stated Gaussian exponentials. The ratio of derivative terms is strictly decreasing for s>0 and gives the credited fixed-width maximizer, including equality. For k>k0, writing H=s_*²/w²=A L gives H′=Ah(T−L) with h>0. The numerator of (L−T)′ has the stated quartic with one sign change and one positive root. Because L−T is negative at k0 and tends to positive infinity, its unique zero above k0 proves strict unimodality, with both endpoint limits zero on the positive interval. At the root k→∞ in the small-p limit, L=T→1 and L=log(pk/2)+o(1); this gives k_peak∼2e/p and s_*∼r_peak∼w√(p/(2e)). An independent bisection at p=1/2 gave k_peak≈7.1551191742 and spacing≈0.6796510696. The frozen verifier and certificate were inspected, not executed; finite tests do not prove the general claim. The repaired clarification that optimal coverage rises with width follows since each trial probability rises almost surely for fixed s, and the smaller-width optimizer is feasible at the larger width. The unique peak is of the spacing curve, not of coverage.

value.rationale: Even as optimal detection probability increases with sensor width, the best physical spacing first increases then decreases. The exact interior peak and limiting gap of twice the width provide a structural design benchmark for comparing sensor widths under a common habitat and baseline response. This is neither the already-covered co-location threshold nor a recommendation to choose width for maximal coverage or estimation precision.
